main_text.p: rent, & memoratis Macedonum & Achæorum recentibus beneficiis, Ætolorum autem nuperis atrocibus maleficiis, majori parti populi persuaserunt, ut existimarent, in societate illorum esse manendum, ab horum fœdere abstinendum; effeceruntque ab ephoris, qui tunc erant, adiuti, ut in eam sententiam decretum scriberetur. Quà re efferati partium adversarum principes, & secum frementes, qui statum talem ferendum sibi non putabant, stimulati tum Achæorum odio, tum prædarum cupiditate, facinus animis conceperunt scelestissimum. Erat in more Lacedæ-moniis à majoribus per manus traditum, solenni die, cum sacrum fiebat in æde Minervæ Chalciacæ, cui præsentes adesse, & sacrum peragere omnes simul ephoros oportebat, universos, quibus ætas justa erat, in armis pompam ducere juxta ædem eandem. Ea pompa cum duceretur, juvenes quidam conjurati, à principibus factionis conducti subito in ædem irrumpentes, quæ ab omni memoriâ tutum confugium & asylum esse solet hominibus etiam facinorosis, capitisque pœnam promeritis, ephoros omnes sacris operantes ad ipsam Deæ mensam atque aram trucidarunt. Immane scelus omnem mo-dun-

page.notes: The catchword "dun-" is the start of the next page's first word, read from the bottom right corner. The small, faint marks at the bottom right beside the catchword are show-through from the reverse side and are not transcribed. The red ink smear over "sententiam" in the middle of the page is a stain. "Quà re" is printed with the accent on the a; I read it as printed. The line "Immane scelus omnem mo-" is a full line that ends with a hyphen and continues in the catchword "dun-", so the paragraph runs on to the next page.
